title: Robust coherent reuse: linear samples with one-quarter malformed tolerance

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). Algorithm RCR-1/4 in proof.md uses q=128(n+1) source registers and threshold r=q/4. Under the fixed-batch marginal replacement model in proof.md Section 2, with at most floor(q/4) malformed positions and the remaining joint marginal exactly rho_s tensor-powered over all good positions, it recovers the full s with unconditional probability >49/64>2/3. All four resource bounds hold jointly on every execution branch for this same algorithm and configuration, with constants independent of N, s and the allowed joint state. Total charged work is T(N,s)=O(N n^2 log2(n+2)), including sample acquisition, all attempts, exact Clifford+T circuit generation, classical bit operations and indexed accesses. A supported uniform asymptotic envelope for n>=2 is B_T(n)=2^n n^2 log2 n, whose growth index is exactly 1; the operational bound covers n=1.

All four resource bounds hold jointly on every execution branch for this same algorithm and configuration, with constants independent of N, s and the allowed joint state. Peak allocated classical memory is S_C(N,s)=O(n) bits, including input, counters, gate generation and all saved classical information. The envelope B_C(n)=n has growth index exactly 0.

Under the fixed-batch marginal replacement model in proof.md Section 2, with at most floor(q/4) malformed positions and the remaining joint marginal exactly rho_s tensor-powered over all good positions, it recovers the full s with unconditional probability >49/64>2/3. All four resource bounds hold jointly on every execution branch for this same algorithm and configuration, with constants independent of N, s and the allowed joint state. The total number Q(N,s) of acquired source copies on every branch is exactly q=128(n+1), including every malformed copy, and no further copies are acquired for failed candidate tests. Thus Q(N,s)=O(n), with envelope B_samples(n)=n and growth index exactly 0.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). Algorithm RCR-1/4 in proof.md uses q=128(n+1) source registers and threshold r=q/4. Under the fixed-batch marginal replacement model in proof.md Section 2, with at most floor(q/4) malformed positions and the remaining joint marginal exactly rho_s tensor-powered over all good positions, it recovers the full s with unconditional probability >49/64>2/3. All four resource bounds hold jointly on every execution branch for this same algorithm and configuration, with constants independent of N, s and the allowed joint state. The guaranteed malformed-sample fraction is epsilon(n)=1/4 under the fixed-batch marginal replacement model explicitly defined in proof.md Section 2 and the structured error_model. The full-secret success and all four resource bounds above hold uniformly under this promise for every N>=2, s, permitted state omega and permitted subset B. This is a fraction of the actual acquired copies, not a per-copy probability; it includes clean inputs and makes no claim of optimal tolerance.

structured.error_model: Fixed-batch marginal replacement model: before measurements the Q acquired (n+1)-qubit registers have a fixed joint state omega. There exists an unknown fixed subset B of at most floor(epsilon(n)*Q) positions whose complementary joint marginal is exactly the tensor product of ideal rho_s states. The state on B and its correlations with other registers are arbitrary subject to that marginal, may depend on N and s, and may include invalid residue basis states. No source adaptation to measurement feedback is allowed. All registers, including B, count toward Q.
